g1.label: 1 — the flat red ___
g1.why: A desert is the dry, sandy land around Uluru; a dessert is something you eat.

g2.label: 2 — never a tourist ___
g2.why: A place people travel to see is a tourist attraction.

g3.label: 3 — its traditional ___
g3.why: The land was returned to the people who own it — the Anangu, its traditional owners.

g4.label: 4 — both names became ___
g4.why: Official is the adjective; an officer is a person and an office is a room.

g5.label: 5 — temperatures can ___ 45°C
g5.why: Temperatures reach a number; you arrive at a place, not at a temperature.

g6.label: 6 — lose everything in a single ___
g6.why: A drought is a long period with no rain — the opposite of a flood.

g7.label: 7 — nobody is ___ to climb it
g7.why: "Be allowed to do something" means to have permission; "aloud" means out loud.

g8.label: 8 — respect their ___
g8.why: Beliefs is the noun (what people believe); "believes" is the verb form.

g1.label: 1 — the guides ___ the tents
g1.why: Putting the tents up happened before we arrived, so it takes the past perfect.

g2.label: 2 — we ___ four hours
g2.why: One finished action at a stated past time ("last summer") takes the simple past.

g3.label: 3 — she ___ her camera at the hotel
g3.why: Leaving the camera came first and explains the later problem, so past perfect.

g4.label: 4 — after the sun ___
g4.why: After the earlier of two past events, use the past perfect.

g5.label: 5 — the government ___ the land back
g5.why: A single event with a date and nothing earlier to contrast it with: simple past.

g6.label: 6 — the farmer ___ most of his sheep
g6.why: "By the time" signals that the losses happened before the rain came.

g7.label: 7 — he ___ never seen so many stars
g7.why: "Never ... before that night" points back beyond the past moment, so had + seen.

g8.label: 8 — when I ___ the film
g8.why: Seeing the film came first here but the sentence tells the two events in order, so the simple past is the natural choice.

g1.label: 1 — ___ we had booked the flights
g1.why: "After" introduces the earlier event; "until" and "while" would change the meaning.

g2.label: 2 — didn’t start ___ everybody had arrived
g2.why: "Not ... until" means the tour waited for the later moment.

g3.label: 3 — ___ the time we reached the campsite
g3.why: "By the time" is the fixed phrase that goes with the past perfect.

g4.label: 4 — never eaten kangaroo ___ she came
g4.why: "Never ... before" marks the whole time up to her arrival in Australia.

g5.label: 5 — Uluru ___ back to its owners (passive)
g5.why: Uluru receives the action, so the passive is needed — as in the New Zealand unit.

g6.label: 6 — asked tourists ___ climbing (gerund/infinitive)
g6.why: "Ask somebody to do something" takes the infinitive — from the Ireland gerunds unit.

g7.label: 7 — as soon as the sandstorm ___
g7.why: The storm passed first; packing came afterwards.

g8.label: 8 — because he ___ 600 kilometres
g8.why: The driving explains why he was tired later, so it belongs in the past perfect.
